claims.text: HEA coatings on transition-metal matrices exhibit a non-monotonic relationship between ambient temperature and tribological performance.
The initial improvement in wear resistance with temperature is caused by formation of a protective tribo-oxide layer.
Tribological performance degrades sharply once matrix softening and oxide-layer instability become significant.
Dense AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 or CoCrFeMnNi coatings can be deposited on Ti-6Al-4V or 316L substrates by physical-vapor deposition or laser cladding.
The proposed coatings possess high hardness and a stable solid-solution structure at room temperature.
The coated system should be tested from 25°C to 800°C under reciprocating sliding in air.
The proposed test uses dry sliding, a velocity of 0.5 m/s, a load of 10 N, and temperature increments of 50°C.
Temperature-dependent wear is governed by competition between protective tribo-oxide formation and thermal softening of the HEA matrix.
Dislocation climb and cross-slip are responsible for the proposed thermal softening of the HEA matrix.
Wear resistance improves or remains stable over 25°C–400°C.
Frictional heating rapidly produces a continuous, adherent oxide tribofilm that reduces metal-to-metal contact and acts as a solid lubricant.
Above T_crit, reduced Peierls stress and activation of multiple slip systems cause significant matrix softening.
Above T_crit, yield strength falls faster than the tribo-oxide can reform or remain adherent.
Tribofilm breakdown causes increased adhesive wear and plastic deformation of the substrate.
The coefficient of friction decreases as temperature rises to approximately 400°C and then rises sharply above T_crit.
The specific wear rate reaches a minimum near 400°C and increases exponentially above T_crit.
The high-temperature degradation corresponds to a transition from oxidative wear to severe adhesive and abrasive wear.
At 25°C, wear is dominated by mild abrasive and adhesive mechanisms without significant thermal oxide formation.
T_crit occurs when coating yield strength drops below the critical shear stress needed to preserve tribo-oxide integrity and is typically 500°C–600°C for Cr/Al-containing HEAs in air.
Refractory additions such as W or Mo may raise T_crit by improving high-temperature strength.
